resources.string: Persistent status and controls for the user-enabled Freenet node
Quiet notice when a newer APK is published
Charging and Always keep a lightweight foreground controller active while the node waits. Always is best-effort: Android can still stop the node.
Uses Android\'s validated and metered network status, regardless of Wi-Fi, cellular, Ethernet, or VPN. Unmetered blocks cellular and metered Wi-Fi.
Battery limits on — tap to open settings
Battery limits off — tap to review settings
Android can still stop a node that is running. Remove battery and background limits for this app if you want it to stay up.
You are about to open dontkillmyapp.com in the browser.\n\nThat site is not part of Freenet. The Freenet Project is not responsible for its content.
Xiaomi: enable Autostart in Security, set battery saver to No restrictions, allow Background autostart, and lock this app in Recents.
Samsung: set this app to Unrestricted, remove it from Sleeping / Deep sleeping apps, and add it to Never sleeping apps.
Huawei/Honor: App launch → Manage manually, then enable Auto-launch, Secondary launch, and Run in background.
Oppo/Realme: allow Autostart / startup in the security app and let this app run in the background.
Vivo: allow background startup / high background power consumption for this app.
OnePlus: disable battery optimization / background freeze for this app.
Asus: allow Autostart and disable power-saver restrictions for this app.
Some phones add extra battery savers. Open the guide for this manufacturer if the node keeps dying.
Xiaomi Autostart detection is only a hint. It can be wrong, and other Xiaomi limits (battery saver, Recents lock, HyperOS background autostart) are not visible to this app.
Takes effect the next time the network node starts.
A typical desktop Freenet node defaults to a minimum of 25 and a maximum of 200 peer connections. Freenet is still experimental.
The network node is already running. Restart it now to apply a minimum of %1$d and a maximum of %2$d peer connections?
The network node is already running. Restart it now to apply the edited config.toml?
Edits apply on the next node start. If the network node is running, you will be asked to restart. Freenet may rewrite this file on start and drop comments.
No text editor is installed that can open config.toml. Use Edit config.toml instead.
